summary: Phase 11 (SURPLUS sweep + 10-yr SECURE post-death horizon) fully validated. Backend pytest: 24/24 PASSED (added test_phase11_features.py: 6 new tests, kept all 18 prior). Confirmed legacy block now contains all required fields incl. post_death_rows (len=10), horizon_years=10, after_tax_estate_at_death, heir_federal_rate, heir_state_rate. Inherited Roth grows monotonically (tax-free) and inherited Traditional fully depletes by year 10. Headline after_tax_estate_to_heirs (10-yr) > after_tax_estate_at_death. surplus_sweep_to: Taxable vs Cash produces measurably different ending net worth (Taxable=$68.86M vs Cash=$59.15M). Default sweep best label is a valid bracket label and best==ranked[0]. UI verified end-to-end on all 4 tabs: legacy-card shows '10-Year SECURE Horizon' title, all 5 estate-* metrics populate, ComposedChart renders (2 areas + 1 line), surplus-sweep-select / funding-order-select / ira-split-slider / max-annual-conversion all wired and re-run projection. Scenarios save/load/delete preserves withdrawal.surplus_sweep_to and legacy settings (heir_federal_rate=0.24, post_death_years=10).
critical_code_review_comments: projection.py run_projection (~540 lines) is large; the income/RMD/withdraw/legacy helpers are already modularized but the main loop is doing ~10 distinct steps and would benefit from extracting the EOY apply/grow stage into a helper for readability and unit-testability.

_post_death_horizon depletes Traditional with `trad / (years - y + 1)` BEFORE growing the remaining balance (good — mimics start-of-year RMD-like withdrawal), but the order means the last year withdraws the entire remaining balance and the post-withdrawal `trad *= (1 + trad_r)` line grows a zero balance — harmless but worth a comment for clarity.

Heir state rate persists to scenarios but if user blanks legacy.heir_federal_rate (None) only via raw API, the `if 'heir_federal_rate' in lc` branch will sum None+x and crash. Defensive default would be safer (`lc.get('heir_federal_rate') or 0`).

Surplus sweep into taxable adds the entire surplus to basis (correct) but the same EOY appreciation `(r - div_yield)` is then applied to the augmented balance — fine for first year but means the dividend yield on the freshly-swept surplus is implicitly assumed to be paid out as recurring_div in the SAME year (already counted in surplus). Worth documenting in the API contract.
frontend `ttFmt = (v) => fmtUSD(v)` is fine but charts apply it to all axes including year_after_death (integer 1..10) in legacy chart tooltips, which will format '1' as '$1' — minor cosmetic.
/api/insights still returns 200 with '[Error generating insights: ...]' inline on LLM failure; better to surface a structured error so UI can degrade gracefully (carried over from iter3).
